evals.name: micro-code-pagination
evals.prompt:
You're a reviewer I'm spawning as team lead.

Mode: micro
Department: code
Target: the PR in files/review-with-mode/pagination-pr/. pr.md is its description and change.diff is its diff against the base project in files/review-with-mode/project/.
Model slug: eval-model

There's no review interface, so return your findings and completion report to me.
evals.expected_output: A High or Critical finding that getPage uses page * perPage with pages numbered from 1, so page 1 skips the newest 20 orders. A High or Critical finding that export-orders.sh runs rm -rf "$out_dir"/* without checking the argument, so running it with no argument deletes everything under /. No finding against pageCount, whose ceiling division is correct. No design findings. Verdict: changes requested.
assertions: Reports that getPage computes start = page * perPage although pages are numbered from 1, so page 1 skips the first perPage items
Rates the getPage finding High or Critical
Reports that scripts/export-orders.sh runs rm -rf "$out_dir"/* without checking that an argument was given, so with no argument it deletes from /
Rates the export-orders.sh finding High or Critical
Does not report pageCount's Math.floor((total + perPage - 1) / perPage) as a bug
Reports no architecture, module-structure or overall-design findings
Every finding starts with the header [CODE] | By Reviewer Micro (eval-model)
Every finding has Issue, Suggested direction, Severity and Complexity
The completion report gives the verdict changes requested, a confidence, and the reviewed target or version

evals.name: macro-code-refunds
evals.prompt:
You're a reviewer I'm spawning as team lead.

Mode: macro
Department: code
Target: the PR in files/review-with-mode/refunds-pr/. pr.md is its description and change.diff is its diff against the base project in files/review-with-mode/project/.
Model slug: eval-model

There's no review interface, so return your findings and completion report to me.
evals.expected_output: A High or Critical finding that the refund handler imports src/db.ts directly, against the README rule that only services may, and so skips the ownership check in getOrderForUser: any signed-in user can refund another user's order. A finding that it converts money with parseFloat and Math.round instead of toCents, against the README rule, so "0.285" refunds 28 cents instead of 29. A lower-severity finding that the PR adds a refund handler, and a handler-to-storage dependency, without updating architecture/workspace.dsl, which the README asks contributors to keep current. The comment typo "recieve" is not reported. Verdict: changes requested.
assertions: Reports that src/handlers/refunds.ts imports src/db.ts directly instead of going through src/services/, against the README's layering rule
Reports that the refund path skips the ownership check, so a user can refund another user's order
Rates the ownership finding High or Critical
Reports that the handler converts the amount with floating-point maths instead of reusing toCents from src/money.ts
Reports that architecture/workspace.dsl isn't updated for the new refund handler, and rates it below the ownership finding
Does not report the typo "recieve" in the handler comment
Every finding starts with the header [CODE] | By Reviewer Macro (eval-model)
The completion report gives the verdict changes requested

You're a reviewer I'm spawning as team lead.

Mode: inquisitive
Department: code
Target: the PR in files/review-with-mode/pagination-pr/. pr.md is its description and change.diff is its diff against the base project in files/review-with-mode/project/.
Model slug: eval-model

There's no review interface. The other reviewers' findings are in files/review-with-mode/pagination-pr/findings.md. Return your replies and completion report to me.
evals.expected_output: F1 keep: the off-by-one in getPage holds up. F2 drop, with the reviewer's own evidence, e.g. pageCount(10, 5) === 2. F3 needs clarification, with a question about whether a page past the end should be an error. No new findings. Verdict on the reviewed findings: changes requested, because F1 is High.
assertions: Gives F1 the verdict keep
Gives F2 the verdict drop, with its own evidence that pageCount is correct when total divides evenly (for example pageCount(10, 5) === 2)
Gives F3 the verdict needs clarification and asks whether a page past the end should be an error
Posts no new findings of its own
Each reply is keyed to its finding ID and has Verdict and Reason
